page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 12 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 90.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 4 local drives. The processor is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in single-core operations and text processing tasks. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.95 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.24 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2309.0. Multi-core performance is also strong, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16269.0 and static web serving throughput of 46.34 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the integrated hardware accelerators support top-tier text generation speeds of 365.79 tokens/sec for small 135M LLM models, though performance drops to a poor tier of 2.39 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides a balanced resource density for compute-heavy applications that require fast local storage without the added cost of dedicated GPU hardware. The inclusion of 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for database operations, web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale data processing. It is also well-suited for text processing and small-scale language model inference, though large-scale model inference represents a clear performance tradeoff.
